known_facts_book1: The village where the coach finally arrives after fourteen hours of travel through the snow from occupied Rouen.
Home to the Hôtel du Commerce, the inn run by M. and Mme Follenvie, where the whole party is put up.
The Prussian occupying officer is billeted at the same inn and personally blocks the travelers' departure until Boule de Suif agrees to his demand.
The travelers are held here for several days, unable to leave because the officer refuses to let the coachman harness the horses.
The coach only leaves Tôtes, resuming its journey toward Dieppe, the morning after Boule de Suif gives in to the officer.

known_relations_book1.l'officier prussien: Is billeted at the inn here and uses his authority over the village to detain the whole coach.
known_relations_book1.M. et Mme Follenvie: Run the Hôtel du Commerce where the travelers are stranded.
known_relations_book1.Boule de Suif: Is pressured into yielding to the officer here before the party is allowed to leave.
